title: B2+ · L2 — Professional video calls
description: Conducir video calls profesionales: interrumpir educadamente, compartir pantalla, gestionar audio, y facilitar reuniones remotas.

questions.prompt: Reunion de Zoom con 8 personas. Alguien lleva hablando 3 minutos y quieres anadir un dato sin parecer maleducado.
questions.question: You want to interrupt politely on a Zoom call. Choose the MOST professional phrase:
options: Sorry to jump in — could I add something quickly?
questions.explanation: 'Sorry to jump in' es la formula de referencia en video calls anglosajonas para interrumpir sin invadir. 'Jump in' es phrasal verb central en meeting culture — anuncia intervencion breve. Nativos ademas suelen anadir 'quickly' para minimizar la interrupcion percibida. Error hispano frecuente: 'my turn' — suena a nino esperando en el patio. Registro: en UK se anade 'if I may...'; en US basta con 'sorry to jump in'.
examples: Sorry to jump in, but I think we might be conflating two separate issues here. → intervencion analitica
Sorry to jump in there — quick clarifying question before we move on. → minimiza la interrupcion

questions.prompt: Vas a presentar un Google Slide a tu equipo.
questions.question: You're about to share your screen. Which is most natural?
options: Let me share my screen — bear with me.
questions.explanation: 'Let me share my screen' es la frase literal de la interfaz de Zoom/Teams/Meet, adoptada como estandar hablado. 'Bear with me' anadido pide micro-paciencia mientras la app carga — muy idiomatico. Error hispano: traducir 'put my screen' desde 'poner mi pantalla' (calco directo, no funciona en ingles). Nota fonetica: 'bear with me' suena /beəwɪðmiː/, casi una palabra unida.
examples: Let me share my screen so you can see exactly what I mean. → antes de mostrar dashboard
Sharing my screen now — bear with me, my laptop's being a bit sluggish today. → excusa natural por lentitud

questions.statement: 'Can you see my screen?' is a common check before presenting content on a video call.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Es una de las 3 frases mas repetidas en video calls modernas junto con 'you're on mute' y 'can you hear me?'. Verificar antes de presentar previene desperdiciar 2 minutos hablando a una pantalla que nadie ve. Nativos van mas alla: 'Are you seeing the slides or my presenter view?' distingue el modo compartido correcto. Registro totalmente neutro.
examples: Can you all see my screen okay? Just want to make sure before I dive in. → check estandar
Just checking — is my screen showing the slides, or the presenter notes? → check avanzado

questions.prompt: Un colega dejo el microfono abierto y se oyen sus hijos gritando de fondo.
questions.question: Someone's microphone is picking up background noise. What's the polite way to ask them to mute?
options: Would you mind going on mute? There's a bit of background noise.
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind going on mute?' es la formula ultra-educada — question form + explicacion suave ('a bit of background noise' minimiza la culpa). 'Go on mute' es la colocacion nativa oficial (no 'silence yourself' que suena a orden). Alternativa muy nativa: 'pop yourself on mute' (mas casual, UK). Error hispano: traducir 'your microphone is bad' — implica que el dispositivo es defectuoso, no que hay ruido.
examples: Would you mind going on mute when you're not speaking? Just picking up a bit of an echo. → correcto
Sorry to interrupt — could you pop yourself on mute? There's some feedback coming through. → registro UK amistoso

questions.text: I'm going to stop sharing now — let me know if anyone has questions before we move on.
questions.explanation: Frase estandar al terminar de presentar slides. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'stop sharing' se enlaza con /pʃ/ (elision de la /p/ audible + /ʃ/ de sharing), sonando casi /stɒʃeərɪŋ/. 'Let me' se reduce a /lemi/ en hablado rapido (schwa + t-flap). Colocacion: 'move on' = avanzar al siguiente tema, no simplemente 'continuar'.
examples: I'll stop sharing now. Any questions before we jump to the next topic? → cierre de seccion
Let me stop sharing so we can all see each other again face-to-face.

questions.prompt: Llevas 8 minutos hablando en una reunion de 30. Quieres invitar a otros sin sonar arrogante.
questions.question: You've been talking too long and want to give others a chance. Which is best?
options: I'll pause there — happy to open it up to the group.
questions.explanation: 'I'll pause there' + 'open it up to the group' es lenguaje de facilitacion profesional puro. 'Open it up' invita colectivamente sin dirigirse a nadie especifico (evita presionar). 'Happy to...' es filler nativo que suaviza. Registro: 'enough of me' suena a falsa modestia infantil. Colocacion clave: 'open the floor' (aun mas formal, tipico de moderadores en conferencias).
examples: I'll pause there — happy to hear thoughts from anyone in the room. → invitacion abierta
Let me pause and open the floor. Any reactions before we move on? → registro formal de moderador

questions.prompt: Empareja cada frase tipica de video calls con su traduccion:

pairs.left: Let me drop the link in the chat.
pairs.right: Dejame poner el link en el chat.

questions.explanation: Cinco frases de supervivencia en video calls modernas. 'Spotty' = irregular/con cortes (colocacion nativa para wifi malo). 'Drop in the chat' se ha vuelto colocacion fija (no 'put in the chat'). 'Circle back' viene del business jargon y significa retomar. 'Frozen' se aplica tanto a video como a apps colgadas. Todas neutras entre US y UK.
examples: You're on mute — we can't hear you, just moving your lips. → aviso clasico
I'll drop the link in the chat for everyone to check afterwards.

questions.target: Before we wrap up, let me quickly recap the action items and make sure everyone's on the same page.
questions.explanation: Cierre profesional estandar en toda reunion recurrente. 'Wrap up', 'action items', 'on the same page' son las 3 colocaciones corporativas mas usadas en English professional speaking. Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'wrap up,' y 'action items,'. Contracciones obligatorias: 'let me' se reduce a /lemi/, 'everyone's' es una silaba mas fluida que 'everyone is'. Discurso marker 'before' + 'let me' senala transicion suave, no brusca.
examples: Before we wrap, let's make sure everyone's on the same page about who owns what. → cierre US corto
Let me quickly recap so we're all aligned on next steps and no one leaves confused. → cierre exhaustivo

questions.prompt: En una call con el CEO te preguntan por una metrica exacta que no recuerdas. No puedes decir 'no se' sin sonar poco preparado.
questions.question: Someone asks a question you can't answer immediately. What's the professional response?
options: That's a great question — let me get back to you on that offline.
questions.explanation: 'Get back to you offline' es lenguaje corporativo estandar y protector: reconoce la pregunta, promete respuesta, y no pierde tiempo de la reunion buscando datos. 'Offline' aqui NO significa 'sin internet' — significa 'fuera de esta reunion', asincronamente (calco frecuente que confunde). Alternativa nativa: 'let me come back to you on that with proper numbers'. Error hispano: decir 'I don't know' seco — culturalmente en anglo se prefiere prometer follow-up.
examples: Great question — I'll get back to you on that offline with the exact figures. → respuesta pulida
Let me take that offline and come back to you with a proper answer by end of day. → mejor aun: da plazo

questions.statement: In American professional English, 'Let's take this offline' means 'let's discuss this separately, not in this meeting'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Take it offline' es business jargon US 100% establecido: significa 'llevemos esta discusion fuera de esta reunion', normalmente a un 1-a-1 o al chat. NADA que ver con desconectarse de internet — puede ocurrir en un chat de Slack (perfectamente online). Se usa cuando un tema se desvia o es demasiado detallado para todos. En UK se acepta pero suena mas americanizado; alternativa britanica: 'let's discuss this separately'.
examples: This is getting into the weeds — let's take it offline and free up the group. → uso tipico US
Happy to dive into that with you — but let's take it offline to respect everyone's time. → excusa educada

questions.prompt: Como facilitador de la reunion, quieres cerrar una decision buscando consenso sin presionar.
questions.question: You want to check if the group agrees with a decision. Which is most natural?
questions.explanation: 'Does that work for everyone?' es la formula de facilitacion mas usada en anglo — busca acuerdo colectivo sin forzar respuesta positiva. 'Work' aqui = funcionar/servir (no trabajar), colocacion nativa fundamental. Error hispano: 'Is it okay?' es demasiado infantil para business; 'You agree?' presiona demasiado. Registro: variante muy britanica 'Does that suit everyone?' es aun mas educada.
examples: Shall we push the deadline to Friday then — does that work for everyone? → busca consenso
Does that work for you all, or would another time suit better? → UK educado

questions.text: I've dropped the agenda in the chat, so feel free to have a quick look before we get started.
questions.explanation: Abertura clasica de reunion. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'have a' se enlaza como /hævə/, y 'quick look' con catenacion /kwɪkˈlʊk/. 'I've dropped' — present perfect obligatorio: la accion (dejar el link) tiene efecto presente (esta ahi para leerse). Error tipico: usar past simple 'I dropped', gramaticalmente aceptable pero menos elegante. Colocacion 'have a quick look' (UK) / 'take a quick look' (US) — ambas nativas.
examples: I've dropped the deck in the chat if you'd like to follow along as I present.
Feel free to have a look at the agenda before we dive into the first item.

questions.prompt: Un colega senior propone algo con lo que discrepas fuertemente. Quieres oponerte sin ofender.
questions.question: You want to acknowledge someone before disagreeing on a video call. Which is most diplomatic?
options: I hear you, and I see the logic — but I'd push back on one point.
questions.explanation: Formula magistral de disenso profesional: 'I hear you' (valida emocionalmente) + 'I see the logic' (valida racionalmente) + 'but I'd push back on...' (introduce desacuerdo constructivo). 'Push back' es phrasal verb esencial en negociacion — significa oponerse educadamente, no atacar. 'You are wrong' es letal profesionalmente. Registro clave: usa siempre condicional 'I'd push back' (hipotetico, no agresivo) en vez de 'I push back' (categorico).
examples: I hear you, and I take the point about cost — but I'd push back on the assumption that users care. → disenso completo
I see where you're going, though I'd gently push back on the timeline. It feels aggressive. → 'gently' suaviza aun mas

questions.statement: 'Let's park this' means 'let's forget about this permanently'.
questions.explanation: FALSO. 'Park this' significa APARCAR = posponer para retomar despues, jamas descartar. La metafora: un coche aparcado sigue existiendo, listo para volver a usarse. En meeting culture se habla del 'parking lot' — una lista mental o de pizarra donde van los temas que se retoman al final o en otra reunion. Error hispano: confundir con 'drop it' (descartar) o 'forget about it' (olvidar). Muy usado en agiles/scrums.
examples: Let's park this for now and revisit it next week when we have Sarah in the room. → posponer
Great point but off-topic — let's park it in the parking lot and come back to it. → tecnica de facilitacion

questions.target: Thanks everyone for making the time today. I'll follow up with a written summary and the action items by end of day.
questions.explanation: Cierre estandar profesional post-reunion. 'Making the time' — colocacion nativa que reconoce el esfuerzo de asistir (mas calida que 'coming'). 'Follow up' = enviar seguimiento; 'end of day' (EOD) es abreviatura corporativa universal. Ritmo natural: agradecimiento primero (calor humano), luego commitment claro (competencia profesional). Contracciones: 'I'll' obligatoria — 'I will' suena rigido y anticuado en cierre de call.
examples: Thanks so much for the time today — I'll send around notes shortly, hopefully before lunch. → clasico US
Appreciate everyone joining — expect a recap by EOD with next steps clearly marked. → registro ejecutivo
